context_title: BAAI/bge-m3 vs Kingsoft-LLM/QZhou-Embedding-Zh vs nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16 vs jinaai/jina-embeddings-v5-omni-small vs Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B vs Octen/Octen-Embedding-8B vs naver-ai/MuCo-7B vs cara-ai/ALM2Vec

entries.query: BAAI/bge-m3 vs Kingsoft-LLM/QZhou-Embedding-Zh vs nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16 vs jinaai/jina-embeddings-v5-omni-small vs Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B vs Octen/Octen-Embedding-8B vs naver-ai/MuCo-7B vs cara-ai/ALM2Vec
entries.answer:
These models split into three fairly different groups: strong text-only multilingual retrievers, multimodal retrievers, and more specialized Chinese or experimental models, so the “best” choice depends mostly on whether you need text-only RAG, cross-lingual retrieval, or text-image/video retrieval. Based on the available model-card and benchmark information, Octen/Octen-Embedding-8B looks strongest for top-end text retrieval, BAAI/bge-m3 remains the safest lightweight multilingual baseline, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B is the most capable multimodal option in your list, and the others are more niche or less fully documented in the sources I could verify.[1][2][3][4]

## What each model is

BAAI/bge-m3 is a 568M-parameter multilingual text embedding model built for more than 100 languages, with support for dense retrieval, sparse retrieval, and multi-vector retrieval, and it can handle inputs up to 8192 tokens. That makes it unusually versatile for classic search and RAG pipelines where you may want one model that can cover multiple retrieval styles without huge compute cost.[5][2]

Kingsoft-LLM/QZhou-Embedding-Zh does not appear directly in the verified results I found, but the closely related Kingsoft-LLM/QZhou-Embedding model is described as a 7B general-purpose contextual text embedding model built on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, with up to 8k context and claims of first place on MTEB and CMTEB as of August 27, 2025. From that description, it looks especially aimed at strong Chinese and general text embedding performance rather than multimodal retrieval.[4]

nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16 is described in the verified search results as an 8B multilingual text embedding model optimized for RAG, semantic search, and cross-lingual retrieval, with a claim of #1 on the multilingual RTEB leaderboard as of July 2026. That suggests it is likely one of the strongest candidates here if your workload is multilingual text retrieval rather than image-text search.[6][7]

jinaai/jina-embeddings-v5-omni-small was not directly surfaced in the verified pages I found, but a recent embedding comparison article lists Jina models as strong on multimodal and dimension-compression scenarios, while a broader 2026 roundup highlights the Jina family as competitive in retrieval use cases. Because I could not verify the exact v5-omni-small card in the allotted sources, I would treat it as promising but not fully confirmed here.[8][5]

Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B is an 8B multimodal embedding model that accepts text, images, screenshots, videos, and mixed multimodal input, supports 30+ languages, has 32k context length, and supports output dimensions from 64 to 4096. That makes it the clearest fit in your list for multimodal retrieval systems where queries and documents are not just plain text.[1]

Octen/Octen-Embedding-8B is a text embedding model fine-tuned from Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B, with 4096-dimensional embeddings, 32,768-token support in its listed model table, and a claimed 40,960-token max sequence length elsewhere on the same page. Its model card claims #1 overall on the RTEB leaderboard with a Mean(Task) score of 0.8045, which is the strongest directly comparable text-retrieval claim among the models in your list that I could verify.[3]

naver-ai/MuCo-7B is a multimodal embedding model in the NAVER MuCo line, listed as based on Qwen/Qwen2-VL-7B and published as a feature-extraction model. The associated collection describes MuCo as “Multi-turn Contrastive Learning for Multimodal Embedding Model,” so this one appears oriented toward multimodal conversational or multi-turn representation learning rather than plain text-only retrieval.[9][10]

cara-ai/ALM2Vec was only visible through a Hugging Face model index result showing ALM2Vec-PT and ALM2Vec-FT as 8B feature-extraction models. Because I could not retrieve a verified model card or benchmark page for the exact root name cara-ai/ALM2Vec from the sources surfaced here, I would treat it as insufficiently documented for confident production selection based on this evidence alone.[11]

## Practical differences

For pure text retrieval, the strongest verified choices in this set are Octen/Octen-Embedding-8B, Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16, QZhou-Embedding, and BGE-M3, but they occupy different points on the cost-quality curve. Octen and Nemotron are positioned as high-end 8B models with leaderboard-oriented claims, QZhou looks especially strong for Chinese-centric text workloads, and BGE-M3 is much smaller and easier to run while still covering 100+ languages and multiple retrieval modes.[2][6][3][4]

For multimodal retrieval, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B is the most clearly documented option here, because its model page explicitly supports text, images, screenshots, videos, and mixed inputs. MuCo-7B is also multimodal, but the surfaced sources provide less operational detail than Qwen’s card, so Qwen is easier to recommend with confidence from the evidence available.[10][9][1]

## Best fit by use case

| Use case | Best pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Lightweight multilingual text RAG | BAAI/bge-m3 | Small 568M model, 100+ languages, dense/sparse/multi-vector support, long-document handling up to 8192 tokens. [2] |
| Highest-end text retrieval | Octen/Octen-Embedding-8B | Fine-tuned from Qwen3-Embedding-8B and claims #1 RTEB overall with 4096-dim embeddings. [3] |
| Multilingual enterprise-style text search | nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16 | Positioned for RAG and cross-lingual retrieval, with a claim of #1 on multilingual RTEB. [6] |
| Chinese-focused text embedding | Kingsoft-LLM/QZhou-Embedding | 7B text embedding model with strong MTEB/CMTEB claims and 8k context. [4] |
| Multimodal search | Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B | Explicit support for text, image, video, screenshots, and mixed inputs. [1] |
| Experimental multimodal alternative | naver-ai/MuCo-7B | Multimodal embedding direction, but less fully documented in the retrieved sources. [9][10] |
| Under-documented choice | cara-ai/ALM2Vec | Present in model index, but not enough verified detail surfaced for a strong recommendation. [11] |

## Recommended ranking

If I were choosing today for **text-only** production retrieval, I would rank them approximately as Octen/Octen-Embedding-8B first, nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16 second, Kingsoft-LLM/QZhou-Embedding-Zh or its closely related QZhou-Embedding variant third for Chinese-heavy usage, and BAAI/bge-m3 as the best efficiency baseline rather than the absolute best quality model. That ranking reflects the benchmark claims and model sizes visible in the retrieved sources, not a unified head-to-head benchmark run across all eight names.[6][2][3][4]

For **multimodal** retrieval, I would put Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B first because its capabilities are the most explicitly documented and broadest in modality coverage among the retrieved results, with MuCo-7B as a secondary option if your stack specifically benefits from NAVER’s multimodal contrastive setup. The Jina and ALM2Vec entries remain harder to rank responsibly here because the exact model pages were not verified in the surfaced sources.[9][10][11][1]

## Selection advice

Choose BGE-M3 if you want a proven open multilingual baseline that is easier to deploy and cheap enough to use widely. Choose Octen or Nemotron when retrieval quality matters more than model size, choose QZhou when Chinese performance is central, and choose Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B when your documents or queries include images or video rather than just text.[2][3][4][1][6]
